newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius seen poised for higher sugar earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius seen poised for higher sugar earnings.

text.p: Sugar authorities in Mauritius believe the industry remains on course for sharply higher output and earnings in 1996/97.

Hector Espitalier Noel, outgoing president of the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate, told a Syndicate annual general meeting on Friday that net revenues from 1996/97 (July/June) exports were seen rising to 8.1 billion rupees ($393 million), from 6.9 billion in the previous year.
An initial 1996 output forecast of 610,000 tonnes or more was being maintained, compared with about 539,500 in 1995.
"The results recorded as at today after two months of production are encouraging, and enable us to hope for a production of 610,000 tonnes or even slightly better," Espitalier Noel said.

"A production of 610,000 tonnes will enable us to deliver our 1996/97 quota under the (Lome) Sugar Protocol, around 507,000 tonnes, our quota to the United States estimated at 25,000 tonnes like in 1995, our deliveries scheduled under the SPS (Special Preferential Sugar) Agreement of about 75,000 tonnes, and some 4,500 tonnes of special sugars to the traditional buyers in the world market," he added.
Espitalier Noel said 1996 production would be just enough to satisfy export commitments, with the result that white sugar would have to be imported for local consumption, as in 1995.
"Government has authorised the Syndicate to import 36,000 tonnes to 40,000 tonnes of white sugar for local consumption," he said.
Mauritius imported 36,000 tonnes of sugar for local use in 1995 after production, heavily undermined by poor weather, fell short of the levels needed to meet commitments.

"It is unfortunate to note that the lower production in 1995 allowed us to deliver only one contingent of 13,500 tonnes under the SPS Accord when Mauritius was allocated some 90,000 tonnes for this first year," Espitalier Noel said.
Espitalier Noel said receipts from sugar exports to the European Union under the Lome Sugar Protocol went down to 436.67 stg per tonne from 448.58 last June.
He blamed this on the appreciation of sterling against major European currencies. Mauritius sugar exports to the EU are priced in Ecus but proceeds are paid in sterling.
